page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-128 is a flexible general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 instruction set. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, the instance delivers 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, supplying 32 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware allocation couples these processing threads with 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB of memory per provisioned vCPU.

The instance design does not include integrated local NVMe storage or auxiliary GPU coprocessors, focusing strictly on standard compute resources. System persistence and disk operations rely entirely on external network-attached block storage volumes. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress routing. This absence of bundled high-speed local disks or hardware accelerators defines a clear operational tradeoff, directing the instance away from extreme disk IOPS operations or heavy parallel machine learning training in favor of compute predictability.

In terms of resource economics, the VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-128 offers balanced cost efficiency for environments needing predictable x86 thread performance without paying premiums for unused local drive arrays or specialized silicon. The instance provides appropriate density for containerized microservice clusters, enterprise web applications, middle-tier database servers, continuous integration pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.16-128 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered for standard enterprise workloads. It operates on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance provisions 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core, combined with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per thread. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and features zero local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. With no hardware GPU accelerators present, the architecture optimizes resource density and computational predictability rather than graphics or specialized machine learning training. The instance is suited for enterprise applications, multi-tier web serving, intermediate database hosting, continuous integration, and containerized microservice deployments requiring dedicated CPU throughput.
